questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Entries of a Matrix Product Representing a 3x3 System of Equations
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y+2z=5 \\ 2x+6y+5z=22 \\ x-2y-3z=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 22 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 6 & 5 \\ 1 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 22 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-y+z=1 \\ 2z+y+x=-1 \\ 3y-z+x=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & b \\ 1 & c & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}0x-y+z=1 \\ x+y+2z=-1 \\ x+3y-z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=0,\,b=2,\,c=3.$

canonical_examples.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}6x+4y=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -1 \\ 3 & b & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}6x+4y+0z=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, $a=6,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-2.$

$$

$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$

$$
